item.title: ICE Arrests Surge at Airports, Opening New Front in Deportation Drive
item.description: Federal agents are arresting spouses of Americans, tech workers and others whose visas have expired, including many who have active applications to stay in the country.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Aleaziz and Miriam Jordan
item.media:description: Chantal Morales Rojas, a 27-year-old from Ecuador, was detained by plainclothes officers as she tried to board a flight at Denver International Airport on July 20.

item.title: Trump’s Spy Chief Spends Final Hours in Job Boasting of Mass Firings

item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes and Dustin Volz
item.category: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
item.media:description: Bill Pulte, the acting director of national intelligence, has not laid out the goals of his purported reductions.

item.title: As U.S. Pauses Strikes, Iran Is No Rush to Resume Cease-Fire Talks

item.title: The Iran War Just Put Another Key Oil Route at Risk
item.description: Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war have led Saudi Arabia to rely on an alternative route for exporting oil. Our reporter Rebecca F. Elliott explains how that route is now threatened by the Houthis, a Yemeni militia supported by Iran.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott, Paul Abowd, Nikolay Nikolov, Nour Idriss, Stephanie Swart, Rafaela Balster, Lauren Pruitt, Alexandra Ostasiewicz, Samuel Granados and Leanne Abraham

item.title: What to Know About the Kumamoto Earthquake in Japan
item.description: At least one person who was found in a collapsed house was killed, and about 50 others were injured on Tuesday in the southwestern prefecture of Kumamoto.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz
item.media:description: A powerful 6.8-magnitude earthquake rocked southwest Japan on Tuesday, causing fires, damaging historic structures and leaving dozens injured, according to the state broadcaster.

item.title: Gov. Sherrill in the Hot Seat After U.S. Demand for Noncitizens’ Names
item.description: After disclosing that thousands of ineligible people were added to the voter rolls, New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill is trying to bring accountability while resisting President Trump’s narrative.
item.dc:creator: Tracey Tully

item.media:description: Gov. Mikie Sherrill of New Jersey has refused U.S. demands to turn over the names of residents mistakenly listed on the state voter rolls.

item.title: Obama to Headline Democratic Redistricting Fund-Raiser

item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Former President Barack Obama will headline a fund-raiser on Martha’s Vineyard in August to help Democrats gerrymander more congressional maps ahead of the 2028 cycle.
